q: In a circular motion, the object just moves in a circle.
e: True. Circular motion means the object travels on a circular path. That is not yet a whole body spinning about an axis.

q: In a circular motion, the object rotates about an axis.
e: False. Circular motion is travel on a circular path. Rotation of a whole body about an axis is rotational motion.

q: An example of circular motion is artificial satellites going around the earth at a constant height.
e: True. An example of circular motion is artificial satellites going around the earth at a constant height. A satellite at constant height travels on a circle around Earth, which is circular motion.

q: In rotational motion, the object rotates about an axis.
e: True. In rotational motion, the object rotates about an axis. Rotational motion means a body spins about an axis.

q: Rotation of earth about its own axis which creates the cycle of day and night is an example of circular motion.
e: False. Earth spinning on its own axis is rotational motion, not circular motion of a point on a circle. The error is the part about Rotation earth own axis creates cycle.

q: Motion of the blades of a fan is an example of rotational motion.
e: True. Motion of the blades of a fan is an example of rotational motion. Fan blades spin as a whole about the motor axis, so that is rotational motion.

q: Motion of a Ferris wheel in an amusement park is an example of rotational motion.
e: True. Motion of a Ferris wheel in an amusement park is an example of rotational motion. A Ferris wheel turns about its central axle, so the wheel is in rotational motion.

q: A rigid body is a body that does not deform or change shape.
e: True. A rigid body is a body that does not deform or change shape. A rigid body does not deform, so its shape stays the same.

q: A rigid body is a body that deforms slightly when the distance between any two particles within the body changes.
e: False. If particle distances change, the body is not rigid. The error is the part about rigid body deforms slightly distance particles.

q: In a rigid body, no matter how the body moves, the distance between any two particles within the body remains constant.
e: True. In a rigid body, no matter how the body moves, the distance between any two particles within the body remains constant. Particle-to-particle distances stay fixed in a rigid body, whatever the motion.

q: If a rigid body is in rotational motion, all the particles constituting it undergo circular motion about a common axis.
e: True. If a rigid body is in rotational motion, all the particles constituting it undergo circular motion about a common axis. Every particle of a rigid rotor rides its own circle about the same axis.

q: If a rigid body is in rotational motion, only the particles on the surface undergo circular motion about a common axis.
e: False. Every particle of a rigid rotor moves in a circle about the common axis, not only the surface. The error is the part about rigid body rotational motion particles surface.

q: When an object rotates, it can speed up or slow down.
e: True. When an object rotates, it can speed up or slow down. A rigid rotor can raise or lower ω, and then it has angular acceleration.

q: During the time intervals when an object speeds up or slows down, its angular velocity is changing therefore it has an angular acceleration.
e: True. During the time intervals when an object speeds up or slows down, its angular velocity is changing therefore it has an angular acceleration. Changing ω, whether speeding up or slowing down, is angular acceleration α.

q: If an object's angular velocity changes at a constant rate, the angular acceleration is constant.
e: True. If an object's angular velocity changes at a constant rate, the angular acceleration is constant. If ω changes at a steady rate, α itself is a constant.

q: If an object's angular velocity changes at a constant rate, the motion is called the rotational motion under constant linear acceleration.
e: False. A constant rate of change of ω is constant angular acceleration, not linear acceleration. The error is the part about object angular velocity changes constant rate.

q: Rotational variables such as angular displacement, angular velocity, and angular acceleration are applied to analyze the rotational motion for a rigid body about a fixed axis under a constant angular acceleration.
e: True. Rotational variables such as angular displacement, angular velocity, and angular acceleration are applied to analyze the rotational motion for a rigid body about a fixed. θ, ω and α are the rotational variables used to analyse spinning motion.

q: The kinematic equations for rotational motion can be derived in terms of the angular displacement, angular velocity and angular acceleration of the object at any instant of time.
e: True. The kinematic equations for rotational motion can be derived in terms of the angular displacement, angular velocity and angular acceleration of the object at any instant. The constant-α kinematic equations are written in θ, ω and α.

q: The initial angular speed is the magnitude of angular velocity of the object at $t=0$.
e: True. The initial angular speed is the magnitude of angular velocity of the object at t=0. Initial angular speed is |ω| at the starting instant t = 0.

q: The initial angular speed is the magnitude of angular velocity of the object at $t=1$.
e: False. Initial angular speed is the magnitude of ω at t = 0. Initial means the starting instant t = 0, not t = 1.

q: The equations of motion for constant angular acceleration are the same as those for linear motion, with the angular quantities replaced with corresponding linear ones.
e: True. The equations of motion for constant angular acceleration are the same as those for linear motion, with the angular quantities replaced with corresponding linear ones. Angular acceleration α is the rate of change of angular velocity ω.

q: The equations of motion for constant angular acceleration are completely different from those for linear motion with constant acceleration.
e: False. The constant-α equations are analogues of the constant-a linear equations, not a different family. The error is the part about equations motion constant angular acceleration completely.

q: The equations for constant angular acceleration in rotational motion are analogous to equations for constant acceleration in linear motion.
e: True. The equations for constant angular acceleration in rotational motion are analogous to equations for constant acceleration in linear motion. The constant-α rotation equations match the constant-a linear set, with θ, ω, α in place of s, v, a.

q: The relations between linear quantities and angular quantities for circular motion have been studied in Grade 11.
e: True. The relations between linear quantities and angular quantities for circular motion have been studied in Grade 11. Keep the exact quantity, direction or number named in the statement.

q: All particles of an object rotating around the axis of rotation move in a circular path.
e: True. All particles of an object rotating around the axis of rotation move in a circular path. Every particle of a rigid body shares the same axis and travels on its own circle.

q: Only the particles on the outer edge of an object rotating around the axis of rotation move in a circular path.
e: False. Particles at every radius move in circles about the axis, not just the outer edge. The error is the part about particles outer edge object rotating around.

q: All particles of a rotating body move in a circle lying on a plane that is perpendicular to the axis.
e: True. All particles of a rotating body move in a circle lying on a plane that is perpendicular to the axis. Each particle's circle lies in a plane at right angles to the rotation axis.

q: All particles of a rotating body move in a circle lying on a plane that is parallel to the axis.
e: False. Each circular path lies in a plane perpendicular to the axis. Each particle's circle lies in a plane perpendicular to the axis.

q: The centre of rotation of the circular path of a particle in a rotating body lies on the axis.
e: True. The centre of rotation of the circular path of a particle in a rotating body lies on the axis. The centre of that circle sits on the axis of rotation.

q: The relation between arc length $s$ and angular displacement $	heta$, measured in radian, is $s = r 	heta$.
e: True. The relation between arc length s and angular displacement heta, measured in radian, is s = r heta. Angular displacement θ is the angle the body turns, measured in radians in the s = rθ family of equations.

q: The relation between arc length $s$ and angular displacement $	heta$, measured in degree, is $s = r 	heta$.
e: False. s = rθ needs θ in radians, not degrees. s = rθ is valid only when θ is in radians, not degrees.

q: Since the direction of linear velocity is tangent to the path, the linear velocity is also called tangential velocity.
e: True. Since the direction of linear velocity is tangent to the path, the linear velocity is also called tangential velocity. Linear velocity is tangent to the path, so it is also called tangential velocity.

q: Since the direction of linear velocity is perpendicular to the path, the linear velocity is also called radial velocity.
e: False. Velocity is tangent to the path, so it is tangential velocity, not radial. The error is the part about Since direction linear velocity perpendicular path.

q: If the magnitude of the linear velocity changes, the object will have a tangential acceleration.
e: True. If the magnitude of the linear velocity changes, the object will have a tangential acceleration. Tangential acceleration a_T lies along the tangent and changes the speed along the circle.

q: If the magnitude of the linear velocity changes, the object will have a centripetal acceleration only.
e: False. If speed changes there is also tangential acceleration, not centripetal acceleration alone. The error is the part about magnitude linear velocity changes object centripetal.

q: The direction of tangential acceleration is always tangent to the circular path.
e: True. The direction of tangential acceleration is always tangent to the circular path. Tangential acceleration a_T lies along the tangent and changes the speed along the circle.

q: The direction of tangential acceleration is always perpendicular to the circular path.
e: False. Tangential acceleration a_T is tangent to the path, not perpendicular to it. The perpendicular direction is radial.

q: The tangential acceleration of a rotating object is a measure of how fast the tangential velocity changes.
e: True. The tangential acceleration of a rotating object is a measure of how fast the tangential velocity changes. Tangential acceleration a_T lies along the tangent and changes the speed along the circle.

q: The tangential acceleration of a rotating object is a measure of how fast the angular displacement changes.
e: False. Tangential acceleration measures how fast the linear speed changes, through a_T = rα. The error is the part about tangential acceleration rotating object measure fast.

q: The direction of the angular velocity vector is perpendicular to the plane of rotation.
e: True. The direction of the angular velocity vector is perpendicular to the plane of rotation. Angular velocity ω tells how fast the rotation angle is changing.

q: The direction of the angular velocity vector is parallel to the plane of rotation.
e: False. The angular velocity vector lies along the axis, perpendicular to the plane of rotation. The error is the part about direction angular velocity vector parallel plane.

q: The direction of the angular velocity vector is along the axis of rotation.
e: True. The direction of the angular velocity vector is along the axis of rotation. Angular velocity ω tells how fast the rotation angle is changing.

q: The direction of angular velocity is usually specified by the right-hand rule.
e: True. The direction of angular velocity is usually specified by the right-hand rule. Angular velocity ω tells how fast the rotation angle is changing.

q: The direction of angular velocity is usually specified by the left-hand rule.
e: False. Direction of ω is given by the right-hand rule. Use the right-hand rule: fingers curl with the rotation and the thumb gives ω.

q: To use the right-hand rule, wrap the right hand around the axis of rotation so that the fingers are pointing in the direction of rotation.
e: True. To use the right-hand rule, wrap the right hand around the axis of rotation so that the fingers are pointing in the direction of rotation. The right-hand rule sets the sense of the angular velocity vector along the axis.

q: In the right-hand rule, the thumb points in the direction of the angular velocity vector.
e: True. In the right-hand rule, the thumb points in the direction of the angular velocity vector. Angular velocity ω tells how fast the rotation angle is changing.

q: In the right-hand rule, the fingers point in the direction of the angular velocity vector.
e: False. In the right-hand rule the thumb points along ω; the fingers curl with the rotation. The error is the part about right-hand rule fingers point direction angular.

q: When the angular velocity is increasing, the angular acceleration vector points in the same direction as the angular velocity.
e: True. When the angular velocity is increasing, the angular acceleration vector points in the same direction as the angular velocity. Angular acceleration α is the rate of change of angular velocity ω.

q: When the angular velocity is increasing, the angular acceleration vector points in the opposite direction to the angular velocity.
e: False. When ω is increasing, α points in the same direction as ω. The error is the part about angular velocity increasing acceleration vector points.

q: When the angular velocity is decreasing, the angular acceleration vector points in the opposite to the angular velocity.
e: True. When the angular velocity is decreasing, the angular acceleration vector points in the opposite to the angular velocity. Angular acceleration α is the rate of change of angular velocity ω.

q: When the angular velocity is decreasing, the angular acceleration vector points in the same direction as the angular velocity.
e: False. When ω is decreasing, α is opposite to ω. The error is the part about angular velocity decreasing acceleration vector points.

q: An object that moves in a circle at constant speed $v$ is said to experience uniform circular motion.
e: True. An object that moves in a circle at constant speed v is said to experience uniform circular motion. In uniform circular motion the speed is constant, but velocity still changes direction so a_C is present.

q: An object that moves in a circle at varying speed $v$ is said to experience uniform circular motion.
e: False. Varying speed on a circle is nonuniform circular motion. The error is the part about object moves circle varying speed said.

q: In uniform circular motion, the magnitude of the velocity remains constant.
e: True. In uniform circular motion, the magnitude of the velocity remains constant. In uniform circular motion the speed is constant, but velocity still changes direction so a_C is present.

q: In uniform circular motion, the direction of the velocity remains constant.
e: False. On a circle the velocity direction continually changes even if speed is constant. The error is the part about uniform circular motion direction velocity remains.

q: In uniform circular motion, the direction of the velocity continuously changes as the object moves around the circle.
e: True. In uniform circular motion, the direction of the velocity continuously changes as the object moves around the circle. In uniform circular motion the speed is constant, but velocity still changes direction so a_C is present.

q: The change in direction of velocity constitutes an acceleration.
e: True. The change in direction of velocity constitutes an acceleration. Acceleration is change of velocity, so a turning velocity is still an acceleration even at constant speed.

q: An object revolving in a circle is continuously accelerated, even when the speed remains constant.
e: True. An object revolving in a circle is continuously accelerated, even when the speed remains constant. Direction change on the circle is centripetal acceleration a_C = v²/r.

q: An object revolving in a circle is not accelerated if the speed remains constant.
e: False. Changing direction means there is still centripetal acceleration at constant speed. The error is the part about object revolving circle accelerated speed remains.

q: The acceleration directed toward the centre of the circle is called centripetal acceleration or radial acceleration.
e: True. The acceleration directed toward the centre of the circle is called centripetal acceleration or radial acceleration. Centripetal acceleration a_C points to the centre of the circle and has magnitude v²/r or rω².

q: The acceleration directed toward the centre of the circle is called tangential acceleration.
e: False. The acceleration toward the centre is centripetal acceleration, not tangential. The error is the part about acceleration directed toward centre circle tangential.

q: Centripetal acceleration is denoted by $a_c$.
e: True. Centripetal acceleration is denoted by a_c. Centripetal acceleration a_C points to the centre of the circle and has magnitude v²/r or rω².

q: Centripetal acceleration is called radial acceleration since it is directed along the radius towards the centre of the circle.
e: True. Centripetal acceleration is called radial acceleration since it is directed along the radius towards the centre of the circle. Centripetal acceleration a_C points to the centre of the circle and has magnitude v²/r or rω².

q: The triangle CAB is geometrically similar to the vector triangle of velocities.
e: True. The triangle CAB is geometrically similar to the vector triangle of velocities. Similar triangles of the radius and of Δv give a_C = v²/r.

q: For uniform circular motion, the centripetal acceleration vector points towards the centre of the circular path.
e: True. For uniform circular motion, the centripetal acceleration vector points towards the centre of the circular path. In uniform circular motion the speed is constant, but velocity still changes direction so a_C is present.

q: For uniform circular motion, the linear velocity vector is tangential to the path.
e: True. For uniform circular motion, the linear velocity vector is tangential to the path. In uniform circular motion the speed is constant, but velocity still changes direction so a_C is present.

q: In uniform circular motion, the centripetal acceleration and linear velocity are perpendicular to each other at every point in the path.
e: True. In uniform circular motion, the centripetal acceleration and linear velocity are perpendicular to each other at every point in the path. In uniform circular motion the speed is constant, but velocity still changes direction so a_C is present.

q: In uniform circular motion, the centripetal acceleration and linear velocity are parallel to each other at every point in the path.
e: False. a_C is radial and v is tangential, so they are perpendicular at every point. The error is the part about uniform circular motion centripetal acceleration linear.

q: In nonuniform circular motion, an object is moving in a circular path with a varying speed.
e: True. In nonuniform circular motion, an object is moving in a circular path with a varying speed. In nonuniform circular motion the speed changes, so both a_C and a_T are present.

q: In nonuniform circular motion, an object is moving in a circular path with a constant speed.
e: False. Nonuniform circular motion means the speed is changing. The error is the part about nonuniform circular motion object moving path.

q: In nonuniform circular motion, the angular speed of the object is changing and the object experiences angular acceleration.
e: True. In nonuniform circular motion, the angular speed of the object is changing and the object experiences angular acceleration. In nonuniform circular motion the speed changes, so both a_C and a_T are present.

q: Angular acceleration in nonuniform circular motion gives rise to the tangential acceleration which is tangential to the circle.
e: True. Angular acceleration in nonuniform circular motion gives rise to the tangential acceleration which is tangential to the circle. In nonuniform circular motion the speed changes, so both a_C and a_T are present.

q: In nonuniform circular motion, there is tangential acceleration in addition to centripetal acceleration.
e: True. In nonuniform circular motion, there is tangential acceleration in addition to centripetal acceleration. In nonuniform circular motion the speed changes, so both a_C and a_T are present.

q: In nonuniform circular motion, there is only tangential acceleration and no centripetal acceleration.
e: False. A circular path always needs a_C; changing speed then adds a_T as well. The error is the part about nonuniform circular motion tangential acceleration centripetal.

q: An object in nonuniform circular motion has a resultant acceleration that is the vector sum of the centripetal and tangential accelerations.
e: True. An object in nonuniform circular motion has a resultant acceleration that is the vector sum of the centripetal and tangential accelerations. In nonuniform circular motion the speed changes, so both a_C and a_T are present.

q: The resultant acceleration in nonuniform circular motion is given by the vector equation $a = a_c + a_T$.
e: True. The resultant acceleration in nonuniform circular motion is given by the vector equation a = a_c + a_T. In nonuniform circular motion the speed changes, so both a_C and a_T are present.

q: Unlike tangential acceleration, centripetal acceleration is present only in nonuniform circular motion.
e: False. Centripetal acceleration is present in every circular motion, uniform or not. The error is the part about Unlike tangential acceleration centripetal present nonuniform.

q: Centripetal acceleration is present in both uniform and nonuniform circular motion.
e: True. Centripetal acceleration is present in both uniform and nonuniform circular motion. In nonuniform circular motion the speed changes, so both a_C and a_T are present.

q: Unlike tangential acceleration, centripetal acceleration is absent in uniform circular motion.
e: False. Uniform circular motion still has a_C; only a_T is zero when speed is constant. The error is the part about Unlike tangential acceleration centripetal absent uniform.

q: The two acceleration vectors $a_c$ and $a_T$ are perpendicular to each other.
e: True. The two acceleration vectors a_c and a_T are perpendicular to each other. a_C is radial and a_T is tangential, so they stand at right angles.

q: The two acceleration vectors $a_c$ and $a_T$ are parallel to each other.
e: False. a_C is radial and v is tangential, so they are perpendicular at every point. The error is the part about acceleration vectors parallel.

q: In nonuniform circular motion, $a_c$ is in the radial direction and $a_T$ is in the tangential direction.
e: True. In nonuniform circular motion, a_c is in the radial direction and a_T is in the tangential direction. In nonuniform circular motion the speed changes, so both a_C and a_T are present.

q: The resultant acceleration points at an angle between $a_c$ and $a_T$.
e: True. The resultant acceleration points at an angle between a_c and a_T. The vector sum of a_C and a_T lies between those two perpendicular arrows.
